chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man whose slave married without his permission, so he consummated the marriage with her. Then the master learned of that. He said: 'That is up to his master; if he wishes, he separates them, and if he wishes, he validates their marriage. If he separates them, the woman keeps what she was given as dower, unless he was excessive, in which case she is given an excessive dower. And if he validates the marriage, they remain upon their first marriage.'

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'For the basis of the marriage was disobedience.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He came to something permissible, and he did not disobey Allah. He disobeyed his master, and did not disobey Allah. That is not like coming to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited for him, such as marriage during a waiting period and similar cases.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave marries without his master's permission?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the fiqh of a slave's marriage without master's permission, distinguishing between disobedience to the master (which is not a sin against God) and prohibited acts like marrying during Iddah. The master holds the prerogative to validate or annul the union, with specific rules for dower distribution upon separation. This ruling underscores the unique legal status of slaves in Shia jurisprudence, where their capacity for contract is subject to the master's consent but their marital bond remains valid if consummated.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja’farasws, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who got his slave married without his permission. So he slept with her, then notified his master upon that. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is up to his master, if he so desires to, he effects separation between them, and if he so desires to he allows their marriage. So if he were to separate between the two, so for the woman would be whatever her dower was except if it is excessive, so her dower is a lot of dower’ and if he allows his marriage, so they would both be upon their first marriage’.

So I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It is as if the marriage was (an act of) disobedience’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, he came to something Permissible, and he did not disobey Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. But rather, he disobeyed his master, and did not disobey Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. That is not like them both coming to what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Prohibited unto him from a marriage, regarding a waiting period and such like’.
